newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. weapons envoy Ekeus to visit Baghdad next week.
newsitem.headline: U.N. weapons envoy Ekeus to visit Baghdad next week.

text.p: Chief U.N. weapons envoy Rolf Ekeus expects to visit Baghdad on April 3-5 to discuss Iraqi compliance with Gulf War disarmament resolutions, his spokesman, Ewen Buchanan, said on Wednesday.
The visit will be the latest in a series Ekeus conducts every two months, usually involving talks with Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz and other senior Iraqi officials.

Ekeus, executive chairman of the U.N. special commission (UNSCOM) in charge of scrapping Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, was due to submit a six-monthly report to the Security Council around April 11.
UNSCOM is not yet satisfied it has received a full accounting of Iraq's chemical, biological and ballistic weapons programmes or evidence that all forbidden weapons have been destroyed.

The Vienna-based International Atomic Energy Agency must give similar clearance regarding Baghdad's nuclear arms capacity before the Security Council can consider easing sanctions imposed soon after Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
As an exception to the sanctions, Iraq has been allowed since last Dec. 10 to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies for its needy population.
When Ekeus last visited Iraq in February he obtained Baghdad's long-delayed agreement for a large number of missile engines to be sent to the United States for analysis.

Iraq scrapped and buried the engines without U.N. supervision in 1992. UNSCOM is having them tested to determine whether any forbidden missiles -- those with a range greater than 93 miles (150 kms) -- remain unaccounted for.
